purpose: `%` and `\` in .param expressions and after `key=`: with blanks around the operator an expression (#180), with none an ngspice number token whose rest is ignored (#200)

oracle.derivation: 10 % 3 = 1: R1=1k. 10 \ 3 = trunc(10/3) = 3: R2=3k. 7k % 4k = 3k: R3=3k. 7k \ 2 = 3500: R4=3.5k. Each i(vk)=-1V/Rk. r=2k%3 is the token 2k%3, read as 2k: R5=2k. r=3k\2 reads 3k: R6=3k.
oracle.cross_check: ngspice-45 (ngspice -b) agrees on i(v1) and i(v2) as written, and on i(v3) and i(v4) with r3 and r4 braced ({7k %4k}, {7k \ 2}); unbraced, ngspice refuses r3 with 'unknown parameter (%4k)', as it refuses `r=10 *3`, since it reads no unbraced expression that starts with a digit (dev/research/ngspice-syntax.md §2.1); r5 and r6 as written: ngspice-45 reads r=10%3 and r=10\3 as 10 (measured 2026-10-18), and inpgtok.c ends a token at blank, tab, =, (, ), comma, a sign, *, / and ^ only
